levelMapping: MTS-1 ≈ 0–2 YOE, MTS-2 ≈ 2–4, MTS-3 ≈ 4–6, MTS-4 ≈ 6–8 (SMTS above that). MTS-2/MTS-3 both map near Google L4; at ~3.3 YOE expect an MTS-2 req with MTS-3 possible on a strong loop — recruiters move candidates between MTS-2 and MTS-3 mid-process (one 2026 report was bumped MTS-2→MTS-3 after the first DSA round). 2024–26 India offers: MTS-2 ~30–40L base + ~$26k RSU, MTS-3 ~40–53L base + $38–75k RSU, MTS-4 ~58L + $67k RSU.

process.summary: A conventional but demanding infra-company loop: HackerRank OA (2–3 problems, medium→hard, sometimes CS-fundamentals MCQs), then 2–3 DSA rounds of LC medium/hard with follow-ups that tighten constraints, an LLD/machine-coding round where runnable, thread-safe, modular code is expected (job scheduler, sparse file, caches), an HLD round with infra-flavoured prompts (KV store, backup service, pub-sub, config propagation), and a techno-managerial/hiring-manager round that digs into OS and database internals. OS/concurrency fundamentals (mutex vs semaphore vs spinlock, malloc, fork/signals, kernel vs user mode) are asked inline in coding and debugging rounds rather than as a separate round. Rounds are elimination-style; design skill and code quality are explicit bars — candidates with strong DSA feedback have been rejected on 'low-level design not good enough' and 'code quality could have been better'.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Background, YOE, why Nutanix, CTC expectation, notice period; explains the loop and schedules the OA or first round. Many loops start from LinkedIn outreach or referral; referrals and experienced candidates sometimes skip the OA.
rounds.probes: Level fit (MTS-2 vs MTS-3 decided here and sometimes changed mid-process), availability for F2F drives.

rounds.name: Online assessment (HackerRank)
rounds.what: 2–3 coding problems, LC medium to hard, sometimes proctored. Recurring OA patterns: 0/1-knapsack variant needing meet-in-the-middle (power/quantity), MST (Min Cost to Connect All Points), DP with monotonic deque (Jump Game VI), sliding-window/frequency design, Dijkstra + heap, House Robber-style DP, text justification. Some OAs add MCQs on SQL, Linux, OS, networking and subjective OS questions (fork + SIGKILL process states).
rounds.probes: Harder than typical OAs — multiple reports call 2–3 LC-hard-ish problems in 90–120 min 'tough for the timeline'. Cutoff appears to be most test cases on most problems.

rounds.name: DSA round(s) — usually 2, sometimes 3
rounds.what: 1–2 problems per round on HackerRank CodePair/CoderPad/Google Doc (one interviewer had the candidate code directly on LeetCode). Graphs/topological sort, trees, binary search on answer, DP, heaps, intervals, stacks/greedy-on-strings recur. Some rounds open with CS fundamentals (OS, Linux, networking) or 10–15 min of project discussion.
rounds.probes: Complete, clean, runnable code including headers; dry-run on edge cases; time/space complexity unprompted; follow-ups that tighten constraints (O(1) space, no extra memory, restore the input, thread-safe version). Rejections cite code quality even when both problems are solved.

rounds.name: Debugging / practical round (some loops)
rounds.what: Not universal but well-attested: fix a 2–3 page client-server program to make it thread-safe, find logical bugs in linked-list pseudo-code, or (2025 MTS-1 DevEx-style) clone an open-source database codebase and locate where features (connection pooling, indexing, execution) are implemented.
rounds.probes: malloc internals, write a semaphore, mutex vs spinlock, deadlock conditions, Linux debugging; for codebase navigation — how fast you orient in unfamiliar code.

rounds.name: LLD / machine coding
rounds.what: Design + working code for a focused module: distributed job scheduler, memory-backed sparse file, thread-safe LRU/LFU cache, student-score manager, tracing library, bookmark manager, seat booking. Runnable code in a shared doc/IDE; UML or class diagrams expected on some panels.
rounds.probes: Thread safety, modularity/SOLID, choice of data structures, DB schema for the entities, concurrency follow-ups ('what if deleteNode is called from multiple threads'). Nutanix explicitly weighs this round heavily — a 'mild yes' with weak design feedback ends the loop.

rounds.name: System design (HLD)
rounds.what: Infra-flavoured prompts: key-value DB (CAP, master-slave), database backup service, Kafka-like pub-sub, config propagation across N servers without a central service, write-heavy storage, observability/tracing, Google Drive, chat app. Candidates draw on draw.io/whiteboard. Mostly for MTS-3/4; MTS-2 loops often merge HLD+LLD into one round.
rounds.probes: SPOFs, scalability, replication and consistent hashing, caching strategy (incl. DB-integrated caches), CAP trade-offs, back-of-envelope estimates. The round label (HLD vs LLD) is frequently miscommunicated by recruiters — clarify beforehand.

rounds.name: Techno-managerial / hiring manager
rounds.what: Project deep-dive with cross-questioning, plus technical depth: API design end-to-end (auth, OAuth, SSL), DB sharding and indexing, how Redis works as a distributed cache, Kafka/messaging, OS processes/memory. Standard behavioral questions; sometimes a quick coding exercise (delete node in a linked list, reader-writer code) and salary discussion.
rounds.probes: Depth on your own systems — interviewers push into internals until you run out; leadership/ownership for MTS-3+. Weak answers here have sunk otherwise-positive loops.

process.indiaNotes: Bengaluru is the main engineering hub, with Pune second (NDB and other teams hire in both); MTS-1 through SMTS are hired in India. The India loop matches the US loop in structure, but US (San Jose) reports skew more to Linux internals, file systems and distributed-storage troubleshooting, while India loops lean DSA-heavy with one design round. India-specific quirks: on-site F2F hiring drives in Bengaluru where 3+ elimination rounds happen in one day (seen Apr 2026); interviews scheduled on <24h notice; and chronic HR ghosting/holds — many 2023–26 reports of positive feedback followed by silence, positions closed without notice, or 'backup candidate' limbo for weeks.
process.timeline: 2–6 weeks end to end when it moves; F2F drives compress all technical rounds into one day. Budget extra weeks for post-loop holds — several candidates with all-positive feedback waited 2+ weeks or were ghosted.
tips: Code quality is an explicit bar: a 2026 MTS-2 candidate solved Group Anagrams + LRU Cache cleanly and was rejected for code quality. Write modular, named, exception-safe code in one pass.
Practice thread-safe variants of everything you know: thread-safe LRU, job scheduler, reader-writer, fine-grained locking on linked lists — concurrency follow-ups are Nutanix's signature.
Revise topological sort cold — it is the single most repeated topic (Course Schedule II, alien dictionary, dependency graphs with cycle detection) across 2021–2026 reports.
Prepare OS inline answers: mutex vs semaphore vs spinlock, malloc internals, fork/SIGKILL semantics, kernel vs user mode, paging — they appear mid-coding-round, not in a dedicated round.
Ask the recruiter to pin down each round's format; HLD-vs-LLD mislabeling is the most common complaint in rejected loops.
For HLD, default to infra prompts: state CAP position, replication/leader-follower, SPOFs, and partitioning early; for LLD bring DB schema + UML, not just classes.
OA prep: meet-in-the-middle knapsack, MST, monotonic-deque DP, sliding window, House Robber; expect 2–3 problems in 90 min with little slack.
Don't treat silence as rejection — follow up, but also keep parallel processes; holds and 'position filled internally' endings are common.
process.notes: OA platform is HackerRank (occasionally proctored); interviews on Zoom + HackerRank CodePair/CoderPad, some on Google Docs with dry-run-only execution. Language is normally your choice (C++/Java/Python/Go reported; Go/Python is the main stack on many teams) but isolated reports of an interviewer forcing Java, and Python-automation/DevEx roles get a Python-internals round (decorators, context managers, how dict/set work, Flask/FastAPI). MTS-2 loops sometimes merge LLD+HLD; MTS-3/4 get separate rounds plus heavier design weighting; a 6-round MTS-3 loop (extra KV-store design round) was run in Oct 2025 when the panel couldn't decide. A debugging round appears in some loops (client-server thread-safety, buggy pseudo-code, open-source codebase navigation). No bar-raiser or values round reported. Post-2024 climate: hiring is active in Bengaluru/Pune across MTS-1–4 with regular drives, but offers are negotiated hard (candidates report lowballs), HR communication is poor, and 2022-style offer rescissions are remembered — get the offer letter before resigning.

dsa.title: Sliding-window frequency tracker
dsa.statement: Maintain a fixed-size window of N characters supporting a stream of operations: add a character (evicting the oldest when the window exceeds N), return the character with maximum frequency in the current window, and return all characters whose frequency is exactly 2. Design the structures so each operation is efficient.
dsa.evidence: Q1 of the 90-min SDE OA, Aug 2026.

dsa.evidence: Q2 of the 2026 SDE OA.

dsa.variant: OA wording: a string 'lost characters'; find minimum insertions to restore a palindrome. Also asked as a full interview problem in a 2022 MTS loop.

dsa.variant: Three distinct variants reported: plain (2026 MTS-2 DevEx), thread-safe implementation with a discussion of lock placement (Feb 2024 MTS-2, round 3), and a time/TTL-aware modification (San Jose phone screen). Be ready to extend to LFU and compare policies.
dsa.evidence: Top Nutanix LC-tag problem (100% 6-mo window); reported 2026-08, 2024-02, 2023-10.

dsa.title: Transform array a into b with minimum operations
dsa.statement: Given integer arrays a (length n) and b (length n+1), transform a into b using minimum operations: increment an element by 1, decrement an element by 1, or copy any current element of a to the end of a (done exactly once, since b is one longer). a[i] must end up equal to b[i] for every index. Examples: a=[1], b=[2,3] -> 3; a=[3,3,3], b=[3,3,3,3] -> 1; a=[5,2,1,4,6], b=[4,1,5,4,6,7] -> 8.
dsa.variant: The appended element can be copied at any point, so you minimize |a[i]-b[i]| sums plus the best choice of when/what to copy for b[n]. Candidate failed on an edge case despite a hint.
dsa.evidence: Round 1, MTS-2 loop, June 2026 (rejected).

dsa.title: Book allocation / Split Array Largest Sum
dsa.variant: Asked in the classic Indian 'allocate books to students minimizing max pages' wording — binary search on the answer.
dsa.evidence: Round 1, MTS-2 loop, June 2026; binary-search-on-answer also in 2018 campus OA (tailors/tasks).

dsa.title: Maximize quantity under power budget (knapsack, meet-in-the-middle)
dsa.statement: Given arrays power[i] and quantity[i] for machines/items and a maxPower budget, pick a subset with total power <= maxPower maximizing total quantity. Constraints are set so plain 0/1 knapsack DP is too slow or memory-heavy — the intended solution enumerates subsets of each half and merges (meet-in-the-middle with prefix-max + binary search).
dsa.variant: Recurs across OAs since 2024 under different stories (manufacturing units, servers).
dsa.evidence: Reported in OAs of Feb 2026 (IC4/5), Oct 2024 (MTS-3/4) and Aug 2024 (MTS, 4–6 YOE).

dsa.title: Python internals gauntlet (DevEx / Python roles)
dsa.statement: A 1-hour mixed round for Python-tagged roles: write a recursive string reverse, then a custom decorator that times the recursive function (tricky — the decorator wraps every recursive call); count 1..100 without a for loop; implement a custom context manager; explain how middleware would be implemented in Flask; SQL for 5th-highest salary; design a FastAPI endpoint returning a paginated response with valid/invalid page handling.
dsa.variant: The FastAPI pagination question was re-asked in another round for the same role months later.
dsa.evidence: MTS-2 Python round, reported Mar 2026 (rejected on the decorator + running out of time); Python hash-map internals also probed in a 2023 SDE loop.

dsa.evidence: Same MTS-2 Python round, Mar 2026 (candidate ran out of time to implement).

dsa.title: Currying: multiply(3)(4)() and infinite currying
dsa.statement: Implement multiply(3)(4)() in any language — a function that accumulates arguments across calls and returns the product when called with no argument. Follow-up: generalize to multiply(1)(2)(3)...(n)() (infinite currying with closures).
dsa.variant: Asked to a backend-leaning SDE-2; candidate switched from C++ to JavaScript to express closures.
dsa.evidence: SDE-2 round, Feb 2026.

dsa.evidence: SDE-2 round, Feb 2026; #3 in Nutanix LC tag 6-month window.

dsa.title: Most-accessed resource in any 5-minute window
dsa.statement: Given unsorted web-access logs [accessTimeSeconds, userId, resourceId] (all within one day), return the resource with the most accesses inside any 5-minute (300 s) window, with its count. E.g. accesses of resource_3 at 53760/54001/54060 → ('resource_3', 3); boundary case: window is inclusive of both ends (1199..1202 counts 4).
dsa.variant: Group timestamps per resource, sort, two-pointer per resource; or global sort + windowed multiset.
dsa.evidence: DSA round 1, May 2025.

dsa.title: Function-call graph: longest chain and longest cycle
dsa.statement: Given user-defined functions where each function body calls others (a() calls b() and c()), build the adjacency list of call dependencies, find the longest call chain (deepest path), and if a cycle exists, return the longest cycle. Involves light parsing, DFS with memoization, and cycle detection.
dsa.evidence: Round 2 of a May 2025 MTS-1 loop (position later put on hold).

dsa.title: Reverse-weighted level sum of a tree in one pass
dsa.statement: Given an n-ary (or binary) tree of height h, compute sum(level-1 values)*h + sum(level-2 values)*(h-1) + ... in a single traversal. Trick: total = (sum of all nodes)*h - sum(node.val * (level-1)), both computable in one DFS.
dsa.variant: Jul 2024 MTS-1 variant: multiply each node by its inverted level order and sum; follow-up pushed from per-level arrays to O(1) extra space.
dsa.evidence: R2 of the Feb 2025 MTS-3 onsite (needed hints); R2 of a Jul 2024 MTS-1 loop.

dsa.title: OA pair: rearrangement max of i*(arr2[i]-arr1[i]) and prefix 'score array'
dsa.statement: Q1: given arrays arr1, arr2 (n up to 1e5, values to 1e9), rearrange each freely to maximize sum over i of i*(arr2[i]-arr1[i]), answer modulo 1e9+7 (sort one ascending, the other descending; watch the modulus). Q2: for each i build score[i] by repeatedly adding max(arr[1..i]) to successive prefix elements and summing — reduces to score[i] = i*max(arr[1..i]) + weighted prefix sums, O(n) with prefix arithmetic.

design.title: Route DB clients to the active node among replicas
design.prompt: Design a service that lets clients connect to the currently-active database node given many replicas (leader discovery / failover routing), asked as HLD+LLD.
probes: health checking and leader election (zookeeper-style sessions/watches)
design.evidence: R3 of the Feb 2025 MTS-3 Bangalore onsite (offer).

design.title: Design Google Drive
design.prompt: HLD of a cloud file storage/sync product, followed by behavioral questions in the same round.
design.evidence: R4 of the Feb 2025 MTS-3 Bangalore onsite (offer).

design.title: Design a robust, scalable write-heavy storage system
design.prompt: Open-ended: build a storage service optimized for heavy writes at scale.
design.evidence: R3 of a Dec 2024 Senior-SDE loop (candidate 'could have done better'; HM round later no-showed).

design.title: Design a Kafka-like pub-sub system
design.prompt: HLD of a publish-subscribe/message-queue system, diagrammed on draw.io; interviewer probed single points of failure and distributed scaling.
design.evidence: R3 of the Nov 2024 MTS-3 loop (went well); 'Kafka and messaging' also probed in Dec 2025 MTS-1 HM round.

design.title: API design deep-dive (techno-managerial)
design.prompt: Design an API end to end: request/response modeling, security (public/private keys, SSL certificates), authentication and authorization (OAuth, tokens), then internal workings — how data is stored, how sharding works, how Redis works as a distributed cache (replication, consistent hashing, hot partitions).
probes: Redis as distributed cache: replication + consistent hashing
design.evidence: R4 of the Nov 2024 MTS-2 loop (rejected on this round); similar DB-internals grilling in 2023 MTS-2 R3.

design.title: Test-execution orchestration across user and worker machines
design.prompt: N Linux user machines hold test binaries; M Linux worker machines execute them. Design the system so users can run their tests on workers with exactly one test running on a worker at a time. Interviewer scaled the problem stepwise: 1 user/1 test/1 worker → many users/many tests/many workers.
probes: worker locking — one test at a time
result collection and retries on worker death
design.evidence: R4 of the Jul 2024 MTS-2 Bangalore loop (offer). Very Nutanix-flavored (internal test infra).

design.title: Scale a read-heavy data service (DB-team flavor)
design.prompt: Open-ended: many users request some data X — design and scale the serving system. Interviewer (DB dev team) kept pushing on database-side speedups beyond standard caching.
probes: cache strategies: cache-aside vs read-through; LRU/LFU invalidation
SQL vs NoSQL choice based on ACID/CAP
design.evidence: R3 of the Jul 2024 MTS-1 Bangalore loop (rejected despite strong answers); comments add interviewer wanted more DB-type/ACID/CAP framing.

design.title: Design an employee expense reimbursement tool (SAP Concur)
design.prompt: Employees submit receipts and get reimbursed; include interfaces for managers and the finance team. Full flow: requirements → API design → DB design → estimates → system flow.
design.evidence: R3 of the Feb 2024 MTS-3 Bengaluru loop; the same prompt ran as HLD+LLD in a Jul 2022 MTS-4 loop (selected).

design.title: Design an observability system
design.prompt: HLD of an observability/monitoring platform (metrics/logs/traces ingestion to dashboards and alerts).
design.evidence: R4 of a 2023 MTS-2 Bangalore loop (ghosted after); interviewers expected depth across architecture, DB and monitoring.

design.title: Make an application highly concurrent and low latency
design.prompt: General prompt: given an application, redesign it for high concurrency and low latency — focus on cache design, database type selection, and related HLD concepts.
probes: SQL vs NoSQL for the access pattern
design.evidence: R3 of the Jun 2024 MTS-3 loop (cleared all rounds).

design.title: Twitter feed with trending windows
design.prompt: Design a Twitter-like feed where each user's feed surfaces trending tweets (by likes) over the last 10 minutes and last 24 hours.
design.evidence: Reported by a candidate in a 2022 thread asking about Nutanix's design round.

design.title: Petabyte-scale ETL pipeline
design.prompt: Design an ETL pipeline that is scalable and fault tolerant and handles petabyte-scale ingestion.
design.evidence: 2021 MTS-3 Pune loop (offer); same loop's R2 asked a per-day sorted telemetry store + streaming top-K/bottom-K with heaps.

design.title: Count unique users connected across a distributed service
design.prompt: A service runs on n distributed nodes; count users currently connected. Then: what data structure for uniqueness? Then the twist — no separate server/DB allowed, only the nodes users connect to.
probes: central session store vs gossip/aggregation among nodes
design.evidence: R4 of the Oct 2021 MTS-3 loop (rejected); paired with fine-grained-locking linked-list question.

design.title: Design a UPI payment app
design.prompt: HM-round design discussion: microservices, APIs, load balancing, user/transaction databases, encryption, security, caching for a UPI-style payment app.
design.evidence: R5 of the 2020 MTS-4 Bangalore loop (offer).

design.title: Troubleshoot latency in a distributed storage cluster
design.prompt: Not a build-from-scratch design: users report rising latency but cluster health looks normal — walk through how you'd investigate a distributed storage cluster (very Nutanix-core; asked with Linux internals, file systems, Ceph and performance-bottleneck follow-ups).
probes: metrics to pull first (disk, network, CPU steal)
design.round: Technical rounds of US MTS-3 loop
design.evidence: Jun 2026 Glassdoor MTS-3 San Jose (accepted offer) — more common in US/storage-team loops; good prep for Bengaluru infra teams too.

design.title: Design a distributed rate limiter
design.prompt: Design a distributed rate limiter handling millions of requests/second across multiple data centers.
probes: degradation when the coordination layer fails
design.evidence: Staff backend engineer write-up (Medium, 2024/25); single low-detail source.

lld.title: Distributed job scheduler (machine coding)
lld.prompt: Build a job scheduler: jobs are submitted with a schedule/time, a pool of worker threads executes them when due. 'Distributed' framing, but the deliverable is single-process machine coding with clean interfaces (Job interface with run(), scheduler storing jobs in a time-indexed map or priority queue, dispatch loop).
lld.deliverable: Runnable, thread-safe, modular code (SOLID); discussion of how it would extend to distributed
lld.evidence: R3 of the Oct 2025 MTS-3 hiring drive (cleared); commenters discussed thread-pool + epoch-ms TreeMap designs. Task-scheduler themes also in OA (cost-optimized two-server scheduling, Sep 2025).

lld.title: Memory-backed sparse file class
lld.prompt: Implement a SparseFile class for a huge (100 GB), ~90% empty file held in memory: WriteData(offset, length, data_in), ReadData(offset, length) returning data with NUL for unwritten gaps, EraseData(offset, length). Memory use must stay close to actual data stored (chunked/interval storage, not byte maps). Caller owns buffers; data_in may die after Write.
lld.deliverable: Working class in a shared doc with dry-run tests; discuss storage layout before coding
probes: chunk map vs interval/ordered map of extents
memory overhead per structure (a map<char,int> blows up 4x)
follow-up they ran out of time for: compression of chunks
lld.evidence: Three reports: MTS-2 C++/Go May 2025 R2; standalone Aug 2024 question post; Jul 2024 MTS-2 offer loop R2 (Google Doc, dry-run test cases).

lld.title: Thread-safe LRU cache (and LFU variant)
lld.prompt: Implement an LRU cache, then make it thread-safe and defend the locking scheme. Variants: LFU cache design (Oct 2021 round), two-segment cache where part 1 holds untouched entries and part 2 holds entries touched at least once (sizes n/3 and 2n/3), with full working code for the replacement logic.
probes: what the mutex protects (map + list together)
lock granularity vs a single global lock
lld.evidence: Feb 2024 MTS-2 R3 (thread-safe LRU); Nov 2024 MTS-2 R2 (two-segment variant, 'HLD' label but full code required); Oct 2021 MTS-3 R3 (LFU); 2018 campus design round (LRU→LFU).

lld.title: Command-line archive utility (mini tar)
lld.prompt: Build a CLI tool, no archive/compression libraries: create (recursively archive a folder preserving structure), extract (rebuild the tree), list (all paths in archive), extract-file (one file), and a --verbose flag. Standard library only; handle invalid paths and corrupt archives gracefully.
lld.deliverable: Working program; focus on FS traversal, binary IO, and designing the on-disk archive format
lld.evidence: May 2025 MTS-1 loop (both rounds positive; role put on hold).

lld.title: Student test-score manager
lld.prompt: Class-managing student records (id like UC11A345, name) and per-subject percentage marks; support entering students, entering marks, querying a student's marks in a subject, and finding the top scorer per subject. No DB — class variables only; a main() must load three specified students and answer two queries.
lld.deliverable: Complete runnable code (took ~1.5 h); interviewer happy with full implementation
probes: data-structure choice for two access paths (by student, by subject)
lld.evidence: R3 of the Nov 2024 MTS-2 Bangalore loop.

lld.title: Multi-user paint application
lld.prompt: Design a Windows-Paint-style app: draw shapes (circle, rectangle, square, triangle...), persist a rectangle drawn inside another rectangle at its exact position in the DB, and let multiple users draw on the same canvas seeing each other's changes (Google-Docs-like). Running code expected within the hour.
probes: how to store geometry in the DB
interviewer pushed back on frontend-heavy designs — keep processing on the backend
lld.evidence: R3 of the Mar 2025 MTS-4 loop — negative LLD feedback ended the process two days later.

lld.title: Tracing library + trace backend service
lld.prompt: Design a tracing system to debug live services: (a) a low-overhead client library multiple services embed to record traces/spans, (b) a backend service with APIs to register traces and fetch the complete trace for a user request, viewable in a basic GUI. Must be reliable and persistent to an agreed degree; bonus: scalable.
lld.deliverable: LLD: entities (Trace/Span/method calls), library API, backend APIs, storage schema
probes: trace/span data model and unique IDs across services
overhead budget in the client library (sampling, async buffers)
query APIs: by id, by status, slowest requests
lld.evidence: R4 of the Nov 2024 MTS-3 loop (unfriendly interviewer; candidate rejected).

lld.title: Client-server thread-safety debugging
lld.prompt: Given ~3 pages of client-server code on a Google Doc, make it thread safe: dependencies between client and server on connection close, and a client may open many connections but only N may execute concurrently. Followed by OS grilling: how malloc works, write a semaphore, mutex vs spinlock, other Linux/OS questions.
lld.deliverable: Corrected, thread-safe code + verbal OS answers
lld.evidence: R3 of the Jul 2024 MTS-2 Bangalore offer loop; debugging rounds also in Jul 2022 MTS-4 (fix error-ridden code), Jul 2024 MTS-1 (buggy palindrome-linked-list pseudo-code), Mar 2025 MTS-3 screen (debugging + graph), 2018 campus (mutex/semaphore bugs in producer-consumer).

lld.title: Open-source codebase navigation (DevEx debugging round)
lld.prompt: Clone a real open-source database driver repo live, then locate where features are implemented down to the code block/line: connection pooling, connection logic; then clone the database itself and find the indexing implementation and query execution logic.
lld.deliverable: Live code navigation + explanation; no writing required
probes: how fast you orient in unfamiliar code (grep/tags/tests)
lld.evidence: R2 of the Dec 2025 MTS-1 loop (selected).

lld.title: Bookmark manager across browsers (UML expected)
lld.prompt: LLD of a system managing a user's bookmarks across multiple browsers on a laptop; interviewer expected UML diagrams and interaction flows.
lld.deliverable: UML class + interaction diagrams, design-pattern discussion
lld.evidence: R4 of the Feb 2024 MTS-3 Bengaluru loop (candidate felt it went poorly; loop ended on hold).

lld.title: Office seat-management app (Robin-like)
lld.prompt: Design a seat-booking/desk-management app: data models, services, user roles, then full DB schema including how relations map to tables.
lld.deliverable: Entity/service design + DB schema on whiteboard/doc (1.5–2 h onsite)
probes: design decisions from your own past projects
lld.evidence: R3 of the Oct 2023 MTS-2 Bengaluru loop (very positive feedback; HM no-show ended it).

lld.title: Design Stack Overflow (LLD with code)
lld.prompt: LLD of Stack Overflow discussed thoroughly, with sample Python code written for the core classes.
lld.evidence: R2 of a Mar 2022 SDE-2 Bangalore loop (Hire; candidate left mid-process for Rubrik).

lld.title: Write code for how malloc() works
lld.prompt: Implement a simplified malloc: manage a heap region, allocate/free blocks, track metadata (free lists/headers), handle fragmentation at least conceptually.
lld.evidence: R3 of a Jul 2022 Bangalore MTS loop (selected; offer later rescinded in cost cuts). malloc internals re-asked verbally in the Jul 2024 debugging round.

lld.title: Multiple readers-writers problem (working code)
lld.prompt: Write working multi-reader/single-writer synchronization code; focus on functionality and modularity. Same round also asked delete-nth-node from a linked list.
lld.evidence: R4 of the Jul 2022 Bangalore MTS loop; reader/writer-style concurrency also in the 2018 campus debugging round and Jun 2025 Pune Glassdoor report (multithreading discussion with code implementation and execution).

lld.title: Thread-safe linked-list operations with fine-grained locking
lld.prompt: Delete duplicate-valued nodes from an unsorted linked list recursively and iteratively; follow-up: make deleteNode safe when called from multiple threads — interviewer hinted at per-node (fine-grained/hand-over-hand) locking, then probed what belongs in the critical section and which lock type to use (spinlock vs semaphore vs mutex).
lld.evidence: R4 of the Oct 2021 MTS-3 loop (rejected minutes after).

lld.title: O(1) read/write/delete store with order-statistics extension
lld.prompt: Build a data structure with read, write (insert) and delete all in O(1); then extend it to also return, for a given element, how many stored elements are smaller — in (near-)constant time, and code both versions.
probes: what breaks when adding order statistics (BIT/bucket trade-offs)
lld.evidence: R2 of the 2020 MTS-4 Bangalore loop (offer); round opened with OS boot/memory internals.

lld.title: Airport runway scheduler (OOD)
lld.prompt: OOP design of a single runway serving arrival flights (which hover and can wait only until fuel runs out) and departure flights (with departure times); schedule landings/takeoffs to minimize delay without starving either.
probes: priority rule: fuel deadline vs departure time (EDF-style)
edge case the candidate missed: simultaneous deadlines
lld.evidence: US onsite, Oct 2023 (no offer; candidate fumbled an edge case).

lld.title: UI-component machine coding (frontend/full-stack MTS only)
lld.prompt: Frontend MTS loops replace LLD with 3 rounds of building UI components live on CodeSandbox in any framework or vanilla JS (Mar 2024 MTS-3 frontend offer); a 2026 full-stack loop had one DSA round + one machine-coding round in JavaScript/React, then a design round.
lld.deliverable: Working component; think aloud; modular, performant code
lld.evidence: Mar 2024 frontend MTS-3 (offered, declined); Apr 2026 full-stack loop. Only relevant if interviewing for UI-tagged reqs.
